title: Unions
summary: Unions allow multiple fields to share the same memory location, requiring unsafe code to access.
lecture: In C and C++, unions allow different fields to occupy the exact same memory location.
Rust supports unions with the union keyword. Unlike enums, unions do not store a discriminant tag to indicate which field is currently active.
Writing to a union field is safe, but reading any field requires an unsafe block because Rust cannot guarantee the data matches the requested field type.

example.caption: Reading a field requires unsafe.
